text.text: Central Park is part of daily life in Hulhumalé. People come to walk, exercise, meet friends and sit with family, and the park holds community events.
Masjid al Sheikh Qasim bin Al-Thani was Hulhumalé’s first mosque, and for a time its only one. Its dome made it an early landmark, and many residents still feel close to it.

text.text: The first flats were home to about 1,000 people, one of the island’s earliest communities. With so few people, life was quiet and close-knit, and neighbours soon knew each other.
The first BBQ area became one of Hulhumalé’s main gathering places. Families and friends came from Malé to cook, relax and spend time together, and early residents still remember it.
